title: Cassoulet
subtitle: Languedoc slow-cooked white bean and meat casserole
excerpt: The great dish of Languedoc: a deep earthenware pot of white beans slow-cooked with confit duck, sausages, and pork belly until the beans are creamy and the top has formed a golden crust. Rich, generous, and made for cold weather.

recipe.sourceNotes: Cassoulet is named after the cassole, the deep earthenware dish in which it is cooked, and is the defining dish of Languedoc in south-west France. The recipe is the subject of a famous rivalry between three towns: Castelnaudary, which claims to be the dish's birthplace and uses only pork; Carcassonne, which adds partridge; and Toulouse, which uses its famous pink sausage. All versions share the same logic: haricot or lingot beans (white beans) slow-cooked with meats until deeply flavoured and thickened by the dissolved collagen from the pork skin. The crust that forms on top is traditionally broken and stirred back in up to seven times, each time a new crust forms. The version here uses the Toulouse approach with confit duck, Toulouse sausages, and pork belly.

content.text: Use dried white beans soaked overnight; tinned beans go to mush over the long cooking time. The cassoulet needs enough liquid to cook the beans through, then the liquid reduces to a thick sauce as the top crust forms. Break the crust back in at least twice during cooking to build depth of flavour.

items.preparation: dried white beans, soaked overnight and drained; use butter beans or haricot
good-quality coarse pork sausages or Toulouse-style
confit duck legs if available; or roasted duck legs

content.text: Heat the oven to 160°C / fan 140°C / gas 3. Heat the duck fat in a large flameproof casserole. Brown the pork belly all over, then the sausages, then the duck legs. Remove each as it colours. Fry the onion and carrot in the remaining fat for 8 minutes. Add the garlic, thyme, and tomato purée. Cook for 2 minutes.

Add the soaked beans, tinned tomatoes, stock, and bay leaves. Season with salt and pepper. Nestle the pork belly into the beans. Add enough water so the beans are covered by 2 cm. Bring to a simmer. Transfer to the oven and cook for 1 hour.

Nestle in the sausages and duck legs. Cook for a further 1 hour 30 minutes, breaking the crust back into the beans twice, until the beans are completely tender and a golden crust has formed. The cassoulet should be thick and slightly soupy, not dry. Rest for 10 minutes before serving.
